outcome.answer: Yes—[1] is the closest match. It studies self-training data built by strategically diverse sampling instead of filtering mainly for correctness, and reports that diverse, even incorrect, traces can outperform IID distillation. [3] is also close: it proposes a one-problem-multiple-solutions paradigm and curates maximally diverse solution sets to improve reasoning diversity and pass@k. [2] is related but focuses more on preserving multiple correct solution modes during RLVR than on choosing varied ways to solve a problem in self-training.
